Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Acute infectious gastroenteritis (viral or bacterial)
- Patient Goal(s):  
  • Restore normal bowel function and abdominal comfort  
  • Regain strength and resume normal daily activities including work  
- Clinical Goal(s):  
  • Prevent dehydration and complications through adequate fluid and electrolyte replacement  
  • Monitor symptom resolution within expected timeframe (3–4 days)  
  • Identify any development of red flags requiring further investigation  
- Actions (Patient):  
  • Increase fluid intake, including oral rehydration solutions (e.g., Dioralyte)  
  • Rest and take time off work for 2–3 days as advised  
  • Take paracetamol as needed for fever or discomfort (dose/route/frequency not documented)  
  • Monitor symptoms closely and seek review if no improvement after 3–4 days or worsening symptoms occur  
- Actions (Clinician/GP):  
  • Provide clear verbal and written advice on conservative management including hydration and symptomatic treatment  
  • Recommend follow-up if symptoms persist or worsen  
  • Consider stool testing if indicated on review  
  • Advise time off work to facilitate recovery  

Secondary Problem: Possible food poisoning / toxin-mediated diarrhea  
- Patient Goal(s):  
  • Identify and avoid potential triggers in future diet  
- Clinical Goal(s):  
  • Educate patient on food hygiene and early recognition of symptoms  
- Actions (Patient):  
  • Avoid suspicious or high-risk food sources where possible  
  • Report any recurrent symptoms or outbreaks  
- Actions (Clinician/GP):  
  • Counsel patient regarding safe food practices and risk factors for food poisoning  

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:
- Education Given: Yes  
- Topics Covered:  
  • Nature and typical course of gastroenteritis  
  • Importance of hydration and rest  
  • When to seek further medical review  
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening:  
  • Persistent or worsening diarrhea after 3–4 days  
  • Blood in stools or vomit  
  • Development of high fever or systemic symptoms  
- Coping Strategies:  
  • Adherence to conservative management  
  • Planned rest and hydration  
  • Symptom monitoring and timely reporting

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Acute infectious gastroenteritis (viral or bacterial): High likelihood. Supported by acute watery diarrhea, vomiting onset, recent food exposure, mild systemic symptoms.  
- Food poisoning / toxin-mediated diarrhea: Medium likelihood. Temporal association with Chinese takeaway, symptom pattern; onset timing slightly longer than typical but plausible.  
- Diverticulitis: Low to medium likelihood. Left lower quadrant pain and diarrhea consistent but absence of fever, blood, or prior disease makes it less likely.
